report.title: Oxford Courthouse Square Historic Preservation District — current footprint inventory

scope.definition: All OSM building footprint parts whose polygon intersects at least 18% of its area with the official municipal district boundary, or whose representative point lies within it. OSM parts are grouped by building object ID; shared storefront address units remain separate in the address and survey arrays.

dataSources.title: City of Oxford Historic Preservation Districts
dataSources.usedFor: Current local preservation district polygon; OBJECTID 4 is Courthouse Square District.

dataSources.title: City of Oxford Courthouse Square Historic District Parcels
dataSources.usedFor: Historic inventory descriptions, names, stories, features, material, roof, photo date, HABS references and contributing status; owner and tax attributes excluded.

dataSources.title: City of Oxford 911 Address View Layer
dataSources.usedFor: Current building, floor and unit address points intersecting the district; address points matched to the nearest footprint at <=18 m.

dataSources.title: OpenStreetMap Mississippi extract
dataSources.usedFor: Current rendered building footprint geometries and positive OSM building IDs in public/data/tiles; no OSM names inferred from nearby unrelated structures.

dataSources.title: Microsoft US Building Footprints
dataSources.license: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL)
dataSources.usedFor: Independent imagery-derived geometry comparison only; polygons are not treated as authoritative or copied into current OSM inventory.

dataSources.title: City of Oxford ArcGIS public service catalog
dataSources.usedFor: Reviewed publicly listed services for a standalone City building-footprint layer. Historic district parcels and address points are available; no standalone City building polygon layer was identified in this catalog during this pass.

dataSources.title: City/MDAH Courthouse Square survey observations
dataSources.usedFor: Address-specific materials, stories, roof forms, storefront units and dated photo links.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: c.2015, 4 story, 11 bays (D, WWW, D, WWW, D,WWW, WWW, D,WWW, D,WWW), steel and brick veneer, Contemporary style, mixed use building. Flat roof with flat transom, cast concrete cornice and setbacks on top floor to accommodate roof balconies with wrought iron balustrades and canvas awnings for roofs. Windows axon ground floor are triple, metal frame single lights. Upper floors have 2/2, metal frame d.h. windows with cast concrete sills and lintels Third floor windows have cast concrete arches inlaid in the  wall and quoins below them give the appearance of brick piers. They are topped with inlaid square capitals are cast concrete. The 4th floor windows are metal framed, 3-part stationary windows. Main entrance is incised with two canted entries that are paired, single light metal framed. All the first floor bays have canvas awning and the building name is on neon sign on the west elevation

historicDistrictParcels.Description: ca. 2000, three story  13 bay (W,W,W,W,W,W,WDD,W,W,W,W,W,W), metal frame with brick veneer, Neo-Gothic, multi-office commercial  building. Roof is flat with elastomeric coating, parapet wall is peaked in the center of façade elevation with an inlaid brick circle, below that is a semicircular, multi light fixed light. The parapet coping and top belt course are granite. Engaged brick piers extend from ground to parapet and are topped with cast round balls, Inlaid squares of marble mark a course between first and second and second and third floors. Windows are 4-light, fixed with marble sills and lentils. Center entry is rectangular, ashlar cut granite and a keystone arch curves over the doors. Stoop is granite blocks with wide, low granite balusters. Double doors are single light metal.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: d. 1910, one-story, 3 bay, (DD, WW, DD), masonry construction, Gothic Revival style early 20th century church. Roof is asphalt shingle, cross gable with single-light, boxed eaves with cornice, fixed sash roundels in gable ends. Façade features two square towers, the left side features a bell shaped roof, the one on the right is three stories, has an arched d.h. stained glass window on 2nd floor and arched, wood vent on the 3rd story. The asphalt shingle roof is conical. The centered façade window is curved with a 4-part, fixed light, stained glass window. The entries are located  below the tower on either end and set in a semi-circular arch reveal with paired, single light wood door and a 2-part, stained glass  arched transom.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: ca. 1860, one-story, 3-bay (dd, w, w), brick masonry Gothic Revival church sanctuary, with added Sunday School and office wings. Gable-front roof covered with metal pattern shingles with scalloped vergeboard and fixed, circular stained glass window in gable. Façade features corner square tower with spire covered with metal pattern shingles. Tower has peaked parapet with corbeled modillion cornice. Front and side façades supported by cast-stone, engaged stepped buttresses. Windows are multilight, fixed stained glass set in Gothic arch reveals. Entrance at ground floor of bell tower has multi-paneled double-door set in Gothic-arched reveal. Side Sunday School (ca. 1955) and office (c. 1996) additions with gable and flared hip roof with asphalt shingles, engaged buttresses, 6/6 d.h. wood windows, and multi-panel doors set in segmental-arched surround.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: ca. 1860, one-story, 3-bay (dd, w, w), brick masonry Gothic Revival church sanctuary, with added Sunday School and office wings. Gable-front roof covered with metal pattern shingles with scalloped vergeboard and fixed, circular stained glass window in gable. Façade features corner square tower with spire covered with metal pattern shingles. Tower has peaked parapet with corbeled modillion cornice. Front and side façades supported by cast-stone, engaged stepped buttresses. Windows are multilight, fixed stained glass set in Gothic arch reveals. Entrance at ground floor of bell tower has multi-paneled double-door set in Gothic-arched reveal. Side Sunday School (ca. 1955) and office (c. 1996) additions with gable and flared hip roof with asphalt shingles, engaged buttresses, 6/6 d.h. wood windows, and multi-panel doors set in segmental-arched surround.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: ca. 1886, two-story,  3-bay (WW, DD, WWWW), masonry construction, Romanesque Revival 19th, century government building. Complex gable roof with asphalt shingles, and box cornice, corbeled omission cornice, and conical dormer with two-light casement sash. Gable ends contain a fan-light casement window and a two-light casement with louvered vent and with semi-circular arch reveals in gable ends. Windows on first floor are paired, 1/1 wood sash on left of façade and there is a bank of four windows on the right side are 2/1 full, 2- 1/1 half-lights and a 2/1 full all separated by vertical limestone lintels, The off-center, projecting porch is masonry with a circular entrance topped with a peaked parapet capped with limestone. The paired entry is two, metal frame single-lights topper by a semi-circular transom. The sidelights have been altered to a 4-lgiht stationary window set into wood.

facts.text: Two and one-half story, brick masonry courthouse building with Romanesque Revival influence, built 1885. Complex gable roof covered with asphalt shingles, with box cornice, corbeled modillion cornice, and gable dormer with two-light casement sash. Gable ends contain a fan light casement, and a two-light casement with louvered vent, each set semi-circular arched reveals in gable ends. Windows are 1/1 double-hung sashes with multi-light transoms, some in segmental-arched reveals, a "Palladian" frup of 2/2 and 1/1 double-hung sashes with a fan light transom set in a semi-circular arched reveal, and groups of 2/2 and 1/1 double-hung sashes with multi-light transoms. Entrance set in gable vestibule with semi-circular arched portal, with replacement single-light double-doors and multi-light transom.
The current municipal address is 107 Courthouse Square. MDAH identifies this as the Old Federal Building, now City Hall; it is distinct from Lafayette County Courthouse at 1 Courthouse Square.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: D. 1871, 3-stories, 9 bays (W,W,W, W, D,W,W,W,W), Italianate style masonry courthouse. Stand-up seam sheet metal, complex gable roof with box cornice and a domed clock tower with bracketed gables and semi-circular louvered vents projects from the center of the roof. The original five-bay rectangle was extended in 1952 by additions at each end of one larger bay which repeated the original end wall elevation. Windows are 4/4 d.h. wood sashes. Segmental arched windows at the ground level of the original block change to semicircular arched at the upper level, and both are replaced on the additions by smaller sash, flat head fenestration. Projecting from the center bay of the south and north elevations are pediment porticoes with Corinthian columns raised on arcades scored in imitation of ashlar masonry.	The two original bays on each side of the porticoes are divided by pilasters rising the full height of the structure from the water table to support a bracketed wooden cornice. Center entry is paired, wood with multi-lights and curved multi-light transom.

Off center recessed entry is single light glass with wood frame and rectangular transom. Second entry is far right, and has 2-lgiht, 2-panel metal door. There is a gated passageway to the right of that entry. Storefront added 1990. NC due to alterations.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: ca. 1877, 1.5 stories, 9 bay (W,W,WD,W,W,W,D,W,W),  stuccoed masonry, High Victorian Italianate style, 19th century commercial building. Flat roof with built up asphalt roofing. Mansard style roof with segmental and rectangular parapet projections and corbeled and bracketed cornice with paneled frieze. Windows are 2-light fixed light windows with arched transoms and stucco bulkheads. The  off-center entry has a single light wood frame door and full single light transom and a small rectangular transom. There is a blind, second transom above it that is arched. The was a sympathetic addition added to the west end in 1975 that mimics the material and massing but the three arced bays are small but have kick plates that match the main building. There are two rectangular fixed light windows above that mark the 2nd floor and they have painted arches above them.  This side addition is in keeping with the Secretary of the Interiors Standards.

historicDistrictParcels.Description: ca. 1880, two story, three-bay (D,WWW), stuccoed masonry, Italianate, 19th story commercial building. Flat roof with built up asphalt-shingle with projecting bracketed window-and roof cornices canted storefront entrance;. Restored double wood gallery with chamfered posts on the full length of east elevation. Triple windows are single-light display with multi-light transom and tile bulkheads. facts.text: Two-story, three-bay, brick masonry commercial block with Italianate influence, built ca. 1880. Flat roof covered with built-up asphalt roofing, with a flat and varietal parapet with gooseneck pediment and finials above panel noting "Dry Goods", and corbeled and bracketed cornice. Exterior walls covered with stucco veneer. Windows are 6/6 double-hung sashes, with segmental arched sheet metal lintels. Two-story, side, hip-roofed gallery supported by chamfered posts with an exterior stair. Storefront features single-light transoms, single-light, fixed sash display windowss, tiled bulkheads, and canted corner entrance supported by a cast iron column with a single-light door with a three-light transom recessed in semi-circular arched entryway.

qualityNotes: City parcels describe assessable parcels, not one parcel per building. The inventory therefore treats each OSM building object and each 911 address/unit as separate layers of identity.
A storefront address may share a footprint with neighboring storefront addresses; use municipalSurveyObservations and attached911Addresses to place units across the common facade.
Survey narratives may cover an entire attached block or a particular frontage. They are retained with their own address rather than copied indiscriminately to every footprint part.

The 61-record survey audit contains 15 cases where the 2000 frontage/footprint assignment differs from the current 911 nearest-shell result. Nine survey segments coincide with their source footprint while the 911 point selects a neighbor; six frontage segments also touch the competing shell. These source joins are preserved and explicitly flagged with candidate IDs and segment distances; no automatic reassignment is made.

gameRenderProfile_unverifiedAsBuilt is the game project profile carried along for comparison only; it can include inferred geometry/materials and is not treated as a historic or current measured fact. Prefer municipal survey, parcel descriptions and dated photos for architectural claims.
A roof footprint does not establish rear wall openings, roof heights, interior plan, or current storefront condition. Missing sides and rear elevations are explicitly left unverified.
The Courthouse Square municipal boundary is not interchangeable with the larger 1980 National Register district boundary; see the source memo for both.

Each 911 point is attached to only its nearest eligible footprint within 18 m. This prevents the search radius from duplicating one address across neighboring shells; distinct published suite/floor points are retained.

historicSourceDates.note: The existing MDAH/NPS campus observations contain historic-photo references but do not state the capture dates of the linked images; no undated view is called current or dated.

knownLimitations: The full boundary ring is the named OSM amenity=university polygon used by the project's existing point-membership audit. It is not an official University property line or an SEC legal boundary.

The official map's page-level claim is over 200 buildings across more than 3,400 acres. Its building categories are location points and include complexes, facilities and duplicate sublocations; the claim is context, not an exact local denominator.

The 25 m map-to-footprint join is a spatial association, not proof of one-to-one physical identity. Exact normalized-name matches are also retained with their measured distances for review. Large multi-wing buildings and campus apartment blocks need part-level review.

All 260 footprints inside the named OSM boundary are included, including 100 unnamed forms. Seventy-eight tile features classified as campus lie outside that polygon and are kept as lower-confidence reconciliation candidates rather than being asserted as within the boundary.

The official map also lists South Oxford, airport, field-station and regional locations. They remain in the map-location inventory; geometries outside the local Oxford cluster are unresolved and are not invented.

Parking lots, gates, gardens, monuments and fountains remain map features, not building assets. Garage/structure entries are distinguished and only become 3D candidates when a nearby footprint exists.

Official map media URLs provide image labels but no capture date in the API response. The existing MDAH/NPS reference views are historical/undated, not current appearances. Inspect sources before using as a current visual target.
The August 2026 university update documents active construction and demolition, including Kincannon Site student housing and West Row housing. The local OSM source may lag these changes.
Footprints are current OSM-derived roof outlines, not measured architectural surveys. Existing model heights are estimates, retained as starting values only.

report.method: Group derived Oxford tile footprints by their original shared feature ID. Compare all repeated IDs to the unsplit OSM polygon in the frozen 2026-11-22 source. An original map feature may combine wings. Official facilities missing geometry remain open.

report.method: Check the official campus-map image endpoint for each unique university-hosted URL associated with the mapped footprint inventory. A successful image response establishes availability. Image capture dates were not supplied. Some map images show activities, interiors, partial views or older facilities.
